findings.claim: On Earth, g is about 10 N/kg. The flashcard answer says 'About 10 N/kg (9.8 N/kg more precisely)' and a knowledge check marks 10 N/kg as the value of gravitational field strength on Earth, with '9.8 m/s' offered only as a wrong-unit distractor.
findings.truth: AQA works in 9.8 N/kg. The spec puts free fall at about 9.8 m/s2 and states that the value of g is given in any calculation. The article now says about 9.8 N/kg and explains that the worked examples round to 10 N/kg for simple numbers; the flashcard now gives 9.8 N/kg; the knowledge check distractor '9.8 m/s' becomes '9.8 N/kg' and is the marked answer.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.1.3 ('In any calculation the value of the gravitational field strength (g) will be given') and 6.5.4.1.5 ('about 9.8 m/s2')

findings.claim: The exam tip tells every student to 'always draw a free body diagram first', and the 6-mark practice question requires one, with no tier flag.
findings.truth: Free body diagrams are Higher tier only for this qualification. The tip now asks for a labelled force sketch and states that free body diagrams are Higher tier; the practice question carries a (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.1.4 '(HT only) ... use free body diagrams to describe qualitatively examples where several forces lead to a resultant force'

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper encloses the whole Elastic Potential Energy section (Ee = 0.5ke^2, its worked example) and the paragraph defining elastic and inelastic deformation.
findings.truth: None of this is Higher tier. Forces and elasticity carries no HT flag; the elastic potential energy equation is on the equation sheet for both tiers, and describing the difference between elastic and inelastic deformation is required of all students. The wrapper hid required Foundation content that the same lesson then tests untiered in practice question 3 and knowledge check 4. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.3

findings.claim: A higher-only wrapper hides the key fact that gives v^2 = u^2 + 2as for uniform acceleration.
findings.truth: This equation is given to both tiers on the equation sheet with no HT flag. Foundation students were then asked it untiered in knowledge check 4 and in the 6-mark practice question. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.4.1.5 'Students should be able to apply this equation which is given on the Physics equation sheet' (no HT marker)

findings.claim: The article states flatly that the area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled, practice question 2 asks for it for 2 marks, and the exam tip tells all students to draw a tangent on a curved distance-time graph.
findings.truth: Both are Higher tier only. The article sentence now says 'At Higher tier, the area under the line also gives the total distance travelled'; practice question 2 carries a (Higher tier) prefix; the exam tip's tangent advice now opens 'At Higher tier'. The matching knowledge check row and two flashcards still drill both without a flag - left alone because they sit inside recall sets rather than exam-style items.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.4.1.5 '(HT only) The distance travelled ... can be calculated from the area under a velocity-time graph'; 6.5.4.1.4 '(HT only) ... drawing a tangent'

findings.claim: Knowledge check 3 asks for the word 'inertia' with no tier flag, although the article's inertia box is correctly wrapped as Higher tier.
findings.truth: Inertia is Higher tier only. The knowledge check now carries a (Higher tier) prefix. Two flashcards and one conclusion takeaway still mention inertia untagged; that is exposure, not assessment, so it is left.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.4.2.1 '(HT only) The tendency of objects to continue in their state of rest or of uniform motion is called inertia'

findings.claim: The Vehicle Safety Features section teaches F = change in momentum / time, crumple zones, airbags, seat belts and ABS as examinable Higher-tier content; the exam tip drills the same equation and a 6-mark practice question is wholly about it.
findings.truth: Changes in momentum is separate-Physics-only content. The words crumple, airbag, seat belt and 'change in momentum' appear nowhere in this specification; momentum here stops at p = mv and conservation. Content kept and labelled 'Separate Physics only'; the exam tip now names the equation as Separate Physics only; the practice question carries a (Separate Physics only) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.5 (only 6.5.5.1 and 6.5.5.2 exist); separate Physics 4.5.7.3 'Changes in momentum (physics only)'

findings.claim: The momentum article is correctly wrapped as Higher tier, but practice question 3 (a conservation-of-momentum calculation) and knowledge checks 1 and 4 test momentum with no tier flag.
findings.truth: The whole momentum topic is Higher tier only for this qualification. All three items now carry a (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.5 'Momentum (HT only)'

findings.claim: The required practical is described as using a ripple tank 'to investigate reflection, refraction, and diffraction of water waves', with a separate two-microphone speed-of-sound method attached to it.
findings.truth: Required practical activity 20 is to identify suitable apparatus and measure the frequency, wavelength and speed of waves in a ripple tank and of waves in a solid. Reflection and diffraction are not part of it, and the 'waves in a solid' half was missing. Rewritten to the spec method, keeping the ripple tank set-up and adding the stretched-string measurement.
findings.evidence: spec 6.6.1.2 required practical activity 20 and section 10.2.20 (physics AT4)

findings.claim: A full Diffraction section, a 4-mark practice question, a knowledge check and three flashcards teach diffraction as examinable wave behaviour.
findings.truth: Diffraction is not in this specification and not in the separate Physics specification either - the string 'diffract' does not occur in either document. The physics is correct, so the section is kept and labelled 'Not examined on this course'. Tom may prefer to cut it and reclaim the space for the required practical work.
findings.evidence: grep of both AQA specs: zero occurrences of 'diffract'

findings.claim: Common permanent magnets are made from iron, steel, nickel, or cobalt.
findings.truth: Iron is the classic soft magnetic material: it magnetises and demagnetises easily, which is exactly why the same lesson specifies a soft iron core for an electromagnet. Permanent magnets are made from steel or magnetic alloys. Rewritten to list the magnetic materials as the spec does, then name steel and alloys for permanent magnets.
findings.evidence: spec 6.7.1.2 (magnetic materials: iron, steel, cobalt and nickel) and 6.7.2.1 (electromagnet = solenoid with an iron core); settled fact

findings.claim: The exam tip tells every student to state F = BIl and use Fleming's left-hand rule; practice questions 3, 4 and 6 and knowledge checks 1, 4 and 5 test the motor effect, F = BIl, the commutator and Fleming's rule with no tier flag.
findings.truth: Fleming's left-hand rule, F = BIl and electric motors are all Higher tier only for this qualification; only the electromagnetism section is untiered. The article is wrapped correctly from the equation onwards, but the assessment items were not. The exam tip now opens 'At Higher tier' and all six items carry a (Higher tier) prefix.
findings.evidence: spec 6.7.2.2 "Fleming's left-hand rule (HT only)" and 6.7.2.3 'Electric motors (HT only)'

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches moments (M = Fd, principle of moments), levers, gears and force as the rate of change of momentum, with vehicle safety features, as examinable content in a Combined Science unit.
findings.truth: None of it is in this specification. The words moment, lever, gear and pivot do not occur anywhere in the document; changes in momentum is separate-Physics-only. Every calculation in the lesson is correct, so the content is kept and labelled 'Separate Physics only', with the description relabelled.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: zero occurrences of moment/lever/gear/pivot; separate Physics 4.5.4 and 4.5.7.3 are both marked physics only

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches the law of reflection, specular and diffuse reflection, sound waves, the human hearing range, ultrasound, echo sounding and seismic waves as examinable content.
findings.truth: All of it is separate-Physics-only. This specification's wave sections cover transverse and longitudinal waves, wave properties, the wave equation and electromagnetic waves; reflection appears only as one thing a substance can do to an electromagnetic wave, at Higher tier. Every fact and calculation in the lesson checks out, so it is kept and labelled 'Separate Physics only'.
findings.evidence: spec 6.6.1 and 6.6.2 scope; separate Physics 4.6.1.3, 4.6.1.4 and 4.6.1.5, all marked physics only

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches convex and concave lenses, ray diagrams, magnification, dispersion, colour mixing and filters, and black body radiation as examinable content.
findings.truth: All of it is separate-Physics-only; the word 'lens' does not occur in this specification and neither does 'black body'. The physics is right throughout, including the filter combinations and the 5500 degC solar surface figure, so the lesson is kept and labelled 'Separate Physics only'.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: zero occurrences of lens/black body; separate Physics 4.6.2.5, 4.6.2.6 and 4.6.3, all marked physics only

findings.claim: Increasing the speed of rotation or the strength of the magnet increases both the peak voltage and the frequency of the output from a generator.
findings.truth: A stronger magnet raises the induced peak voltage but cannot change the frequency: the output frequency is set only by how fast the coil turns. Rewritten to separate the two effects.
findings.evidence: settled fact (induced emf peak scales with B, N and rotation rate; output frequency equals the rotation rate)

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches electromagnetic induction, alternators and dynamos, the transformer turns equation Vp/Vs = Np/Ns and transformer construction as examinable content in a Physics Paper 2 unit.
findings.truth: Induction, generators and the transformer equation are separate-Physics-only; the word 'induction' does not occur in this specification. The National Grid is in this qualification but sits in the electricity topic, which is assessed on Paper 1, and this spec adds that detailed knowledge of transformer structure is not required, with only primary and secondary power equality at Higher tier. Content kept and labelled.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.4.3 The National Grid ('Detailed knowledge of the structure of a transformer is not required'); separate Physics 4.7.3 'Induced potential, transformers and the National Grid (physics only)'

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches the solar system, orbits, the life cycle of stars, red-shift, the Big Bang, the cosmic microwave background and dark matter as examinable content.
findings.truth: Space physics is separate-Physics-only; solar system, star, orbit, red-shift and Big Bang do not appear as physics content anywhere in this specification. Every value in the lesson checks out (99% of solar system mass in the Sun, 15 million degC fusion ignition, 2.7 K background, 13.8 billion years, 27% and 68% dark matter and dark energy), so the lesson is kept and labelled.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: zero occurrences of solar system/red-shift/Big Bang; separate Physics 4.8, marked physics only

findings.claim: Lesson 9 is wholly outside this qualification and is published live at tier 'both'.
findings.truth: The label is the safe interim fix. Options: (a) keep it as a labelled extension lesson, which the edits assume; (b) move it to the separate-sciences board where it is examined and drop it here; (c) retire it. Recommendation: (a) now, (b) at the next rebuild - it also duplicates the momentum teaching in lesson 5, so a Combined student meets the same out-of-scope material twice.
findings.evidence: see F13

findings.claim: Lesson 10 is wholly outside this qualification and is published live at tier 'both'.
findings.truth: Same three options as lesson 9. Recommendation: keep and labelled for now, move to the separate-sciences board at the next rebuild. This one is the strongest candidate for a move rather than a retirement, because the content is accurate and complete enough to serve a separate Physics unit as it stands.
findings.evidence: see F14

findings.claim: Lesson 11 is wholly outside this qualification and is published live at tier 'both'.
findings.truth: Same options. Recommendation: keep and labelled now, move at the next rebuild. Note that the infrared emission and absorption work that IS examined here already lives in lesson 7, so nothing is lost to Combined students by moving this lesson.
findings.evidence: see F15

findings.claim: Lesson 12 is largely outside this qualification, and the part that is inside it (the National Grid) belongs to a different paper.
findings.truth: Options: (a) keep it labelled as an extension lesson; (b) move the induction, generator and transformer-equation material to the separate-sciences board and fold the National Grid paragraphs into the Paper 1 electricity unit, which already teaches the National Grid; (c) retire it. Recommendation: (b), because the National Grid content is duplicated with the Paper 1 unit and a Combined student revising it here is revising Paper 1 material inside a Paper 2 unit.
findings.evidence: see F17

findings.claim: Lesson 13 is wholly outside this qualification and is published live at tier 'both'.
findings.truth: Same options. Recommendation: keep and labelled now, move at the next rebuild. Two of its six practice questions (the Hubble constant calculation and the cosmic microwave background extended response) go beyond even the separate Physics spec, so a move should be paired with a question rewrite.
findings.evidence: see F18 and F28

findings.claim: Five of the thirteen lessons (9 to 13) are wholly or largely outside this qualification, while several statements the spec does require for this paper are not taught anywhere in the unit.
findings.truth: Missing in-scope material: distance versus displacement as a scalar-vector pair (6.5.4.1.1) is never taught - lesson 3 opens at speed; radiation dose and the sievert, with 1000 mSv = 1 Sv (6.6.2.3), is absent from lesson 7; radio waves produced by, and inducing, oscillations in electrical circuits (6.6.2.3, HT only) is absent; and the compass as evidence that the Earth's core is magnetic (6.7.1.2) is absent from lesson 8, which uses the compass only for plotting. The four required practicals for this paper are all named and, after F9, all described correctly. Filling the content gaps means authoring new sections and re-narrating, which is beyond a surgical edit.

findings.claim: Lesson 6 teaches the law of reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) and explains refraction by a change of wave speed, both untiered.
findings.truth: The law of reflection is separate-Physics-only, and the speed-change explanation of refraction is Higher tier only in this qualification; drawing a ray diagram for refraction is the part that is untiered. Not edited: reflection is one sentence and a glossary entry, and refraction genuinely is on the course, so a scope label here would cost more clarity than it buys. Worth a look if lesson 6 is ever rebuilt.
findings.evidence: spec 6.6.2.2 '(HT only) Some effects, for example refraction, are due to the difference in velocity'; separate Physics 4.6.1.3

findings.claim: Lesson 9 repeats lesson 5's momentum teaching almost word for word, including the identical 1200 kg / 800 kg collision worked example and the same crumple zone, airbag and seat belt material.
findings.truth: Not a factual error - both copies are correct - but a student who works through the unit meets the same out-of-scope safety-features section twice. Worth folding into one lesson at the next rebuild.
findings.evidence: lessons 5 and 9 content_html

findings.claim: Knowledge check 4 reads 'The National Grid transmits at high voltage to reduce energy losses caused by _____ in the cables' and marks 'current' correct, with 'resistance' as a distractor.
findings.truth: Resistance in the cables is also a true cause of the losses, so a student who understands P = I squared R can be marked wrong for the right reason. Not edited because the lesson is out of scope for this qualification anyway; if lesson 12 is kept, reword to 'so that the _____ in the cables is low'.
findings.evidence: settled fact (P = I^2 R depends on both current and resistance)

findings.claim: Practice question 3 asks students to calculate the Hubble constant from a recession speed in km/s and a distance in Mpc, and practice question 6 is a 6-mark extended response on the cosmic microwave background.
findings.truth: The arithmetic is right (6000 / 80 = 75 km/s/Mpc) but neither topic is in the AQA GCSE specification at all: separate Physics covers red-shift qualitatively and names dark mass and dark energy only, with no Hubble equation and no background radiation. Not edited because the whole lesson is already labelled out of scope.
findings.evidence: separate Physics 4.8.2 Red-shift (physics only)

findings.claim: Lessons 5, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 all have an empty glossary_terms array although their content carries dfn tooltips with definitions.
findings.truth: The in-lesson tooltips still work, but the glossary panel is empty for six of thirteen lessons. Not a factual error and not fixable by a surgical text edit; flagged so it can be picked up by the glossary backfill.
findings.evidence: raw fields

findings.claim: The lesson 3 description is 101 characters.
findings.truth: The house validator limit is under 100 characters, so this row may block a later validation run. It is not a factual error, so it is not edited here; every other description in the unit is inside the limit, including the five rewritten for scope labels.
findings.evidence: house validator limit

summary: Thirteen lessons checked; 30 findings (13 HIGH, 10 MEDIUM, 7 LOW; 18 FIX, 6 ADJUDICATE, 6 NOTE) and 41 edits. Every worked example in the unit recomputes correctly - resultant forces, work done, spring constant and elastic potential energy, acceleration and v^2 = u^2 + 2as, stopping and braking distances, momentum collisions, wave speed, F = BIl, moments, magnification and the transformer turns ratio all check out, so the yield is not random error but the same two build faults found in Physics Paper 1. First, scope: lessons 9 to 13 (moments, levers and gears; reflection, sound and ultrasound; lenses, colour and black body radiation; induction and transformers; space physics) are wholly or largely separate-Physics-only, which is 38% of the unit, and lesson 5's vehicle safety section and lesson 6's diffraction section are off-spec too; all are accurate, so all are kept and labelled, with placement left to Tom. Second, tier: the higher-only wrapper is on the wrong sections - it hides elastic potential energy and elastic deformation in lesson 2 and v^2 = u^2 + 2as in lesson 3, both required of Foundation students, while genuinely Higher-tier material (momentum, the motor effect, F = BIl, Fleming's rule, the area under a velocity-time graph) is tested untiered in twelve practice questions and knowledge checks, now prefixed. The only outright factual errors are the generator key fact in lesson 12 (a stronger magnet does not raise the output frequency), permanent magnets said to be made from iron in lesson 8, the ripple-tank required practical described as a reflection and diffraction investigation in lesson 6, and g given as 10 N/kg in lesson 1 where AQA uses 9.8 N/kg.
